question_text: In triangle ABC, $\text{AB} = 15\text{ cm}$, $\text{AC} = 12\text{ cm}$, and $\text{A}\widehat{\text{B}}\text{C}$ measures $30^\circ$.

subparts.stem: Find the two possible values of $\text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B}$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up the sine rule for $\sin\text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B}$

subparts.solution: $\frac{\sin\text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B}}{15} = \frac{\sin 30^\circ}{12} \implies \sin\text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B} = \frac{15\sin 30^\circ}{12}$. Thus $\text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B} = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{15\sin 30^\circ}{12}\right)$ or its supplement $\implies \text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B} \approx 38.7^\circ \text{ or } 180^\circ - 38.7^\circ \implies \text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B} \approx 38.7^\circ \text{ or } 141.3^\circ$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The ambiguous case of the sine rule occurs when finding an angle, since $\sin(\theta) = \sin(180^\circ - \theta)$.
step_by_step: Set up the sine rule using opposite pairs.
Find the principal angle using inverse sine.
Determine the supplementary angle by subtracting from $180^\circ$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Omitting the obtuse solution when both angles are geometrically possible.

subparts.stem: Given that $\text{B}\widehat{\text{A}}\text{C}$ is acute, find its measure.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The sum of angles in a triangle is $180^\circ$.
step_by_step: Select the obtuse angle $\text{A}\widehat{\text{C}}\text{B} \approx 141.3^\circ$ from part (a).
Subtract the known angles ($30^\circ$ and $141.3^\circ$) from $180^\circ$ to find angle $A$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the acute angle from part (a) instead of the obtuse angle specified by the condition.
